newsitem.title: UK: Japanese tourist takes wrong turn to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Japanese tourist takes wrong turn to Turkey.

text.p: There were no minarets, mosques or bazaars and the pervading smell was vinegary fish and chips, not Byzantine spice.
But Japanese tourist Kumiko Tsuchida was convinced she had reached her rightful destination after using extremely broken English to ask directions in London to Turkey.

A long rail journey later and Tsuchida was exploring Torquay, a seaside resort in southwest England whose sole claim to fame is as home to fictional Basil Fawlty, the manic hotel owner invented by British comic John Cleese.

"I kept saying 'Turkey, Turkey'. But because of my pronunciation, they put me on a train to Torquay," she told the Daily Mail newspaper. "I thought it was a long way to the airport but when I asked people 'Turkey? Turkey?' they told me I was on the right train."

Despite the signs of supreme Englishness -- double-decker buses, dowdy weather and shabby shopfronts -- Tsuchida could not believe she had gone wrong, so helpful were the train conductors along the way.

"English people are very helpful, very kind and polite," she said. Polite -- but wrong. It fell to police to intervene after the dazed tourist was spotted wandering the streets by night, suitcase in hand.

"She told officers in broken English that she had been on the train so long she genuinely believed she was in Turkey already. She even thought she had been through the Channel Tunnel," said a police spokesman.
After a confusing night in an old people's hostel, Tsuchida -- who had only Turkish money on her -- was whisked back to London to resume her journey by air.

Said a consular officer at the Japanese embassy: "I don't know what she made of Torquay versus Turkey but I offered her help over the phone, in Japanese of course, and she said she was fine. This is the first such mixup but I just laughed. Everybody would enjoy this joke, no?"
